body:
DESIGN PROPOSAL: the cost blend carries the support it rests on. bd-01M177SHFXZKMR8K39BPC9K6FF.
m1, for review by cursor-grok-storymodel4s before any code. No candidate exists; nothing is built.

=== THE DEFECT, stated narrowly ===

  source cell   = sum over PRESENT terms + functionPrior   -- SHRINKS when a term is absent
  external cell = externalFloor, a flat constant           -- does not move (cost.scala:703-706)

A unit we could measure on FEWER dimensions looks MORE ANCHORABLE, because its source cost falls
against a floor that stays put. It is NOT a source-versus-source defect: present-term sets are
uniform within a row - the absence conditions are properties of the recall UNIT, not the node - so
the offset cancels in the softmax and in Viterbi. I reported it as source-versus-source earlier and
withdrew that.

=== THE PROPOSAL ===

1. blend scales the weighted sum UP TO ELIGIBLE SUPPORT:

     cost = functionPrior + (sum over present of w_t * x_t) * (W_eligible / W_present)

2. THE PRIOR STAYS OUTSIDE THE SCALING. It is a per-discourse-function constant, not a term; it
   was calibrated against the sum and scaling it would distort the function priors for exactly the
   units whose terms went missing. Stated because it is the one arbitrary-looking choice here.

3. CostBreakdown RECORDS what it did:
     supportWeight  = W_present / W_eligible   -- 1.0 when everything eligible was measured
     eligibleTerms  = the set that could have been measured for this cell
   This is what stops it being a hidden convention. The imputation travels with the value.

=== WHY ELIGIBLE AND NOT ALL TERMS ===

Measured, default weights:

  scale over ALL terms       5-term 1.3594   6-term 1.2985   -- nothing is ever bit-identical
  scale over ELIGIBLE terms  5-term 1.0469   6-term 1.0000   -- EXACTLY 1

Chart and Structural are absent for the WHOLE corpus - WOG contains no charts. Scaling as though
they should have been measured invents a dimension the data cannot have, inflates every source cost
by a third against an unmoved floor, and flips the row to External. I built that version, measured
it, and reverted it.

=== HOW ELIGIBILITY IS DERIVED, WITHOUT TOUCHING Estimate ===

Estimate has two arms, Observed and Missing; it cannot say "never eligible" - that is
bd-01M16DBEH9PKER423BZ47ZKBMV, deferred. But the cost model already holds the answer:

  the five dense terms   always eligible
  Structural             eligible iff a provider was supplied - `structural` is a field of
                         DefaultLocalCostModel and defaults to StructuralDistance.missing
  Chart                  eligible iff the node carries chart evidence, which the view knows

If Estimate later grows an Ineligible arm, this derivation is replaced by the typed one and the
recorded field keeps its shape. The two compose; neither blocks the other.

=== IT IS STILL AN IMPUTATION, AND THAT IS THE POINT ===

Scaling assumes the unmeasured terms behave like the average of the measured ones. That is an
assumption and it can be wrong. The difference from today is not that one imputes and the other
does not - TODAY IMPUTES ZERO COST, which reads as perfect agreement, and nobody chose that. The
difference is that this one is named in supportWeight, recorded per cell, and refusable.

=== TWO LAWS, AS ASSERTIONS ===

  L1  a cell whose eligible terms were all measured is BIT-IDENTICAL to today.
  L2  dropping a term that could not be measured must not change which state wins for that unit.
      Today's code FAILS L2 - that is the positive control, not a hope. L2 holds only under the
      imputation above, and supportWeight is how a consumer knows it was used.

=== WHAT I AM NOT PROPOSING ===

- Not a mean. A mean would force recalibration of floor, mismatch, distortion penalty and priors
  against WOG, which is fitting the model to the fixture we validate on.
- Not touching externalFloor. It is the deeper asymmetry - a constant that does not participate in
  the term structure, which is why three separate fixes today all foundered on it - but it is a
  separate question and I would rather not conflate them.
- No recalibration of any weight.

=== OPEN, AND I WANT THE REVIEWER ON THESE ===

- Is Chart eligibility a per-CELL property (this node has evidence) or a per-VIEW one (any node
  does)? I lean per-view: "no charts exist" is a property of the corpus, whereas one node lacking a
  chart while others have one is a genuine per-cell absence. But they differ on mixed views and I
  have no fixture with one.
- Should supportWeight below some threshold make the cost REFUSE rather than scale? That is the
  abstention question, and I think no - the aligner must produce a posterior - but it deserves an
  argument rather than my assumption.
